extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent owners, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO examiners/administrative patent judges handling appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and content requirements for taking an appeal from a USPTO examiner to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (now PTAB), preparing and filing the notice of appeal and appeal brief, timing/fee rules, docketing, and subsequent judicial review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of Board
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 6: Establishment and composition of the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (Director, Deputy Commissioner/Deputy Director, Commissioners, and administrative patent judges); judges must be persons of competent legal knowledge and scientific ability. Each appeal shall be heard by at least three members of the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also defines 'Board' (per 37 CFR 41.2) for final and non-final actions and who constitutes a 'Board member'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative handling and docketing readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte appeals and related documents filed prior to docketing are forwarded to the Patent Appeal Center for processing. The appeal is docketed only if ready (no return to examiner required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ready for docketing: (A) an appeal number assigned; (B) Board issues docketing notice identifying appeal contents and filing dates; (C) appeal assigned to master docket or individual APJ. If not ready, the case is returned to examiner with order indicating reason and no appeal number assigned until ready.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Appeal Center review responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Appeal Center reviews notices of appeal, pre-appeal brief requests, examiner’s answers, and reply brief acknowledgements, and notifies appellant of defects in notices of appeal or pre-appeal brief requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Center will return applications to the examiner for corrections when appropriate (e.g., unsigned examiner's answer containing a new ground of rejection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special case continuation through appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application was made special and advanced out of turn, it remains special throughout prosecution including appeal, subject to diligent prosecution by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to make special after appeal may be addressed to the Board but will not be granted unless the brief has been filed and the same showing required by the Director under 37 CFR 1.102 is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may appeal (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 134 and 37 CFR 41.31: (a) a patent applicant any of whose claims has been twice rejected may appeal; (b) a patent owner in reexamination may appeal a final rejection; (c) a third-party requester in inter partes reexamination may appeal certain final decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules specify timing references for pre- and post-November 29, 1999 reexaminations and cross-reference applicable CFR sections for time periods and fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal fees and payment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees are required on filing an appeal and on filing an appeal brief and on requesting an oral hearing (fee amounts listed in statute/regulation and MPEP references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees must accompany filings as required (e.g., notice of appeal fee per 37 CFR 41.20(b)(1); appeal brief fee per 37 CFR 41.20(b)(2)); failure to timely pay fees may render the notice or brief defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing Notice of Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of appeal must be filed within the time period provided under 37 CFR 1.134 (the reply period set in the last Office action) and may be filed up to 6 months from the Office action date with an appropriate petition and fee under 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notice of appeal may be filed after any claim has been twice rejected, and the 'twice rejected' condition need not be within the same application (Ex Parte Lemoine). Notices may not be filed while RCE in effect; special rules for reexamination appeals apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement for notice of appeal (exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: The signature requirement of 37 CFR 1.33 does not apply to a notice of appeal filed under 37 CFR 41.31; unsigned notices of appeal are permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: But unsigned notices may have unintended adverse consequences for other unsigned items submitted with the notice (e.g., unsigned authorization to charge fees), potentially making the filing unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal must be from rejection of all claims under rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal, when taken, must be taken from the rejection of all claims under rejection which the applicant or owner proposes to contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions not affecting the merits may be required to be settled before appeal considered; the appeal cannot cover matters outside the rejected claims the appellant intends to contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective notice of appeal procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice of appeal is defective (e.g., not timely filed, fee missing, not proper reply because claims not twice rejected), the Office will notify applicant of non-compliance using Form PTOL-461 and indicate defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will indicate when a notice is not a proper reply or other specific defects; the Office may return the application to the examiner for correction when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief filing deadline and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Per 37 CFR 41.37(a), appellant must file a brief within two months from the date of filing the notice of appeal, accompanied by the fee set forth in § 41.20(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file the brief with required fee within this period will result in dismissal of the appeal; the time period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136 and, for reexamination, under 1.550(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and order requirements for appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Per 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(i)-(x): the brief shall contain, under appropriate headings and in the order indicated: (i) real party in interest; (ii) related appeals/interferences; (iii) status of claims and identification of those appealed; (iv) status of amendments after final rejection; (v) summary of claimed subject matter; (vi) grounds of rejection to be reviewed; (vii) argument with citations; (viii) claims appendix; (ix) evidence appendix; (x) related proceedings appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants not represented by a registered practitioner need only substantially comply with certain paragraphs (see rule). Each item must be present; exceptions and limited compliance allowances are specified for pro se appellants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of claimed subject matter and identification of means/steps
rubrics_metrics.description: For each independent claim involved and each dependent claim argued separately, the brief must provide a concise explanation of the subject matter, referring to the specification by page/line and to drawings by reference characters; every means-plus-function and step-plus-function element must be identified and the corresponding structure/material/acts in the specification set forth with references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement implements 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph, and is mandatory for the summary section of the brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of grounds of rejection to be reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief must contain a concise statement of each ground of rejection presented for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This focuses the Board's review to the stated grounds; only grounds presented will be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument format, waiver, and grouping of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument must state contentions for each ground of rejection with citations; any argument not included in the brief or reply will be refused unless good cause shown. Each ground must be treated under a separate heading. Claims may be argued separately or as a group; failure to separately argue grouped claims constitutes waiver of separate consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple claims are grouped, Board may select a single claim from the group to decide the appeal for that group; merely pointing out what a claim recites is not an argument for separate patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims appendix requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing a copy of the claims involved in the appeal must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims appendix helps the Board and examiner quickly identify the contested claim language; follow appendix formatting rules in the MPEP/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence appendix and prohibition on referencing unentered evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: An evidence appendix must contain copies of any evidence submitted pursuant to §§ 1.130–1.132 or other evidence entered by the examiner and relied upon by appellant, along with a statement indicating where in the record the evidence was entered. Reference to unentered evidence is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 41.33 for treatment of evidence submitted after appeal; evidence relied upon by the examiner as to grounds of rejection may also be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related proceedings appendix requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing copies of decisions rendered by a court or the Board in any proceeding identified as related must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to related appeals/interferences or judicial proceedings must be supported by copies of decisions in this appendix as required by paragraph (c)(1)(ii) and (c)(1)(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: No new or non-admitted amendments or evidence in brief
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For amendments/affidavits/evidence filed after final action but before or same date as filing appeal, see § 1.116; for evidence after filing the appeal see § 41.33.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant brief procedure and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If a brief does not comply with paragraph (c), appellant will be notified of reasons for non-compliance and given time to file an amended brief. Failure to file an amended brief within the set period, or filing one that does not overcome the stated reasons, will result in dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office provides specific notification of defects and an opportunity to cure before dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of appeal after prosecution reopened
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant wishes to reinstate an appeal after prosecution is reopened, appellant must file a new notice of appeal in compliance with 37 CFR 41.31 and a complete new appeal brief in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37; previously paid appeal fees will be applied to the new appeal if no final Board decision has been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appeal fees increased since they were paid, appellant must pay the difference. The new brief must be filed within two months of the new notice of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time measurement for filing appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office date of receipt of the notice of appeal (not the date on Certificate of Mailing) is the date from which the two-month period to file the appeal brief is measured. If filed under 37 CFR 1.10 using USPS 'Express Mail Post Office to Addressee', the date of deposit with USPS is the date of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If notice of appeal filed by Express Mail under 1.10, the 'date in' on Express Mail label is the receipt date; see MPEP §§ 512–513 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time to file appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The two-month period can be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a); if not available, under 1.136(b) for extraordinary circumstances. Petitions to TC with fee required; extensions in excess of 5 months generally require extraordinary circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time extended is added to original period (calendar day) rather than adjusted for weekend/holiday; form paragraphs provided for grant/denial of extension under 1.136(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to timely file appeal brief generally results in dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for limited exceptions (e.g., declaration of an interference or suggestion of claims for an interference and timely copying), the appeal ordinarily will be dismissed if the brief and the appeal brief fee are not filed within the period provided by 37 CFR 41.37(a) or properly extended time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A brief must be filed to preserve appellant’s right to appealed claims notwithstanding circumstances such as petition to Director, amendments that don't dispose all issues, receipt of examiner letter suspending prosecution without withdrawing final rejection, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing an appeal brief without a prior notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: When an appellant files an appeal brief without filing a notice of appeal first, the Office should treat the appeal brief as both a notice of appeal and an appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this situation, the brief must be filed within the reply period set in the last Office action and the fees for both filing a notice of appeal and an appeal brief must be paid in compliance with 37 CFR 41.31 and 41.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals to the Federal Circuit: notice, timing, and filing methods
rubrics_metrics.description: When appealing to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, appellant must file a written notice of appeal in the PTO directed to the Director within the time specified in 37 CFR 1.304; a copy of the notice and docket fee must be filed with the Clerk of the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notice is timely if it actually reaches the PTO within the time or is mailed by Express Mail under 37 CFR 1.10. The notice should be filed by mail to 'Mail Stop 8' (Director, P.O. Box 1450), by Express Mail under 1.10, or by hand to the Office of the Solicitor at the specified address; the notice should not be mailed to the Director/Board/examiner or the Solicitor's court papers address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of court papers on the Director / Solicitor
rubrics_metrics.description: All service copies of papers filed in court proceedings in which the Director is a party must be served on the Solicitor of the Patent and Trademark Office; service may be by hand to the Office of the Solicitor or by mail to 'Mail Stop 8'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule citations from Fed. R. Civ. P. 5(b) and Fed. R. App. P. 25(b) explained; noncourt papers mailed to the Solicitor's mail service address will be returned to sender—do not use that address for noncourt filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office procedure following Federal Circuit decision (mandate effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Federal Circuit decision and issuance of the mandate, the mandate is entered in the application/reexamination/interference file and marks the conclusion of the appeal; the application/file is returned to the appropriate PTO official for further proceedings consistent with the mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all claims stand rejected, proceedings are terminated on the issue date of the mandate; if some claims allowed, termination applies only to rejected claims; remand or reopening of prosecution may occur as directed by the court's decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review — handling of administrative file and amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: During judicial review, the administrative file is not opened to the public by the PTO unless otherwise available; any amendment can be admitted only under 37 CFR 1.198.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will prepare and transmit the record and grounds for its decision to the Federal Circuit as required by statute; procedures for handling the file after court disposition are set out (see MPEP § 1214.06 etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 145 civil actions: evidence and issues
rubrics_metrics.description: In a 35 U.S.C. 145 civil action (district court), the plaintiff may introduce evidence not previously presented to the PTO but will be precluded from presenting new issues absent a reason of justice; new evidence not admissible if available but withheld due to fraud, bad faith, or gross negligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All expenses of proceedings in a 145 action are paid by the applicant. Timely service of complaint and summons on Solicitor, U.S. Attorney for D.C., and Attorney General is required per Fed. R. Civ. P. rules and cited cases.
